messages:
alex (customer): Hey support, running into an install/import issue with the Python SDK after using poetry extras. `poetry install` succeeded but `import redwood` throws ImportError. Also seeing intermittent SSL verify failures in our CI on macOS macbook m1. stack:
```
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx' (/.../.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/__init__.py)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1129)
```
I used `poetry add redwood-sdk[http]` and python 3.10.6. Any ideas?

maya (support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste `python -V`, `poetry --version`, and `poetry.lock` httpx/httpcore entries? Also which macOS version and whether you're using system Python or pyenv/venv?

alex (customer): python -V -> Python 3.10.6
poetry 1.4.2
macOS 13.6 on M1 (arm64). Using poetry-managed venv (no system site-packages). From poetry.lock: `httpx` resolved to 0.22.0, `httpcore` to 0.15.0. redwood-sdk allowed httpx >=0.23 in our pyproject but lock ended up older because another dep pinned it.

maya (support): ok that explains the AsyncClient problem (httpx changed names/exports between 0.22 and 0.23). Two vectors: upgrade httpx to a compatible version, or pin an SDK version that supports 0.22. Which is easier for you?

kevin (engineer): ping — the SDK's http-related helpers expect httpx>=0.23.x (AsyncClient moved/refactored). If poetry.lock resolved 0.22.0 because of a transitive constraint, run: `poetry add httpx@^0.23.3` to force resolution then `poetry lock --no-update` or `poetry update httpx httpcore`. Also note on macOS M1 you sometimes get binary wheels built against a different OpenSSL which can cause the cert verify issue (certifi vs system cert store).

alex (customer): I tried forcing httpx to 0.23.3 and reinstalled, import issue goes away, but now CI tests fail with: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate`. Local env works but CI (github actions macos-latest) fails.

infra-bot: CI job redwood-sdk-tests / macos-setup — 3/3 failed :x: (automated note)

maya (support): For the SSL error on macOS runners, two quick things to try: 1) ensure `certifi` is installed and the runtime is pointing to it, 2) ensure any rebuilt wheels match the OpenSSL used on the runner. Can you run:
```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade certifi
python -c "import certifi, ssl; print(certifi.where()); print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"
```
and paste output?

alex (customer): certifi.where() -> `/Users/runner/.cache/pip/wheels/.../certifi/cacert.pem`
ssl.get_default_verify_paths() shows openssl cert file pointing to system path `/usr/local/etc/openssl/cert.pem` (which doesn't exist on runner).

kevin (engineer): That mismatch is the problem — the Python build on the runner is using a different OpenSSL path than certifi. Workarounds: in your CI before tests run, set `SSL_CERT_FILE` env var to certifi's path, or call `export SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -m certifi)`. Example CI step:
```yaml
- name: Fix macOS SSL certs
  run: |
    python -m pip install --upgrade certifi
    echo "export SSL_CERT_FILE=$(python -m certifi)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
Also rebuild any binary deps on runner arch (or use manylinux wheels). For poetry, you may need `poetry run pip uninstall httpx httpcore && poetry run pip install httpx==0.23.3 httpcore==0.16.0` if binary mismatch persists.

alex (customer): Applied the SSL_CERT_FILE export in CI; tests that hit API pass now. One last thing: are there recommended pinned versions to avoid this in the future? The transitive constraint causing 0.22 was from another in-house package.

kevin (engineer): Recommended pins for stability (our internal compat matrix): `httpx==0.23.3`, `httpcore==0.16.0`, `certifi>=2023.7.22`. Also in pyproject, prefer `redwood-sdk>=1.4,<2.0` (adjust to your org). If you must keep the other in-house package pinned to older httpx, either upgrade that package or use a separate venv for services that need newer httpx.

maya (support): Glad this is unblocked. I'll leave a short KB entry: "Poetry + macOS CI: httpx mismatch -> AsyncClient import error + cert verify failures; fix by pinning httpx/httpcore & setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi in CI." Want us to open a support ticket to follow up on your workspace dependency (we can do dependency surgery with you)?

alex (customer): Yes please open a ticket to help coordinate upgrading the in-house package. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
